title: “Special mercy” as object — prefer saying grace-promises fiducially applied
source_text: XCII. Quod autem multi ex Protestantibus dicunt, misericordiam specialem esse proprium objectum fidei justificantis, per hoc non aliud significare volunt, quam proprium esse fidei justificantis, prout distinguitur a fide historica, ut promissiones divinae misericordiae sigillatim cuique credentium applicet: ea ratione ut ante justificationem peccata sibi esse remittenda confidat, & post justificationem credat sibi esse remissa. Sed quoniam hic loquendi modus obscurus est, & etiam calumniae obnoxius, mallem, quod multi faciunt, ab eo abstinere, & simpliciter dicere potissimum fidei justificantis objectum esse promissiones gratiae, prout sunt assensu practico & fiduciali a credente apprehendendae, & ipsi applicandae, quod eodem recidit.
pass_a_gloss: But when many of the Protestants say that special mercy is the proper object of justifying faith, by this they mean nothing else than that it is proper to justifying faith, as distinguished from historical faith, that it apply the promises of divine mercy seal by seal to each of the believers: in such a way that before justification he trusts that sins are to be remitted to him, and after justification believes that they have been remitted to him. But since this mode of speaking is obscure, and also liable to calumny, I would rather, as many do, abstain from it, and simply say that the principal object of justifying faith is the promises of grace, as they are to be apprehended by the believer with practical and fiducial assent, and applied to himself — which comes to the same thing.
pass_b_english: “Special mercy is justifying faith’s proper object” means: unlike historical faith, it applies divine-mercy promises personally — before justification trusting sins will be remitted, after believing they have been.
The phrase is obscure and open to slander.
Le Blanc prefers (with many): principal object = grace-promises apprehended with practical fiducial assent and applied to oneself — same substance, clearer words.
